scenes.headline: How a design skill turns taste into checks
scenes.sub: Impeccable: instructions for coding agents, and a linter underneath
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Swatch! Impeccable is a design skill for coding agents, with a linter underneath.

scenes.text: The vocabulary is mostly a list of refusals, and about half of them are written as thresholds that code can check on a real page.
scenes.say: Most of its vocabulary is things not to do. About half are written as thresholds that code can check.

scenes.title: What the agent loads, and what checks it

steps.say: The agent loads one skill file, a router that points each command to its instructions.
Before any edit it reads the craft floor: no side stripes, no nested cards, no label above a heading.
When the agent edits a page, a hook runs the detector. Plain code, no model.

steps.note: mechanical rules per edit, the rest when the agent stops
steps.say: Findings go back to the agent. Taste waits until it stops.

scenes.title: Three ways to read a page
scenes.say: The detector reads a page three ways.

items.say: Pattern matching over source, fast but blind to styles set in code.

items.text: A static HTML and CSS engine
items.say: Its own HTML and style engine.
Or a real Chrome, measuring painted boxes and pixels.

scenes.title: How AI beige becomes a rule
scenes.say: Take the beige everyone complains about.

parts.say: Every channel has to be near white.
And red beats blue, but only a little. Even ivory counts.

steps.note: side stripe, kicker, italic serif, beige
steps.say: The project shows four tells: a side stripe, a label above the heading, italic serif, and beige.
A vague headline has no rule. Only the model can judge that.

scenes.label: Catalogue entries, sorted by what they measure

scenes.title: Keeping the thresholds honest
scenes.say: A loop keeps the thresholds honest.

items.text: Run every rule on real sites
items.say: Run every rule on real websites.
Rarely harmful rules stop failing the build.

scenes.text: Writing taste as a number makes it checkable. Testing each number against real pages keeps it honest.
scenes.mark: Testing each number against real pages
scenes.say: Writing taste as a number makes it checkable. Testing it on real pages keeps it honest.

recap: A skill file routes to refusals
A detector checks them, no model
scenes.say: Refusals, a detector without a model, and real websites to keep it honest.
